question: An investigator is studying the effect that mutations in different parts of the respiratory tract have on susceptibility to infection. A mutation in the gene encoding for the CD21 protein is induced in a sample of cells obtained from the nasopharyngeal epithelium. This mutation is most likely to prevent infection with which of the following viruses?

paths: (Complement Receptor Type 2)-INTERACTS_WITH->(Dendritic Cells, Follicular)-LOCATION_OF/PART_OF->(Virus)-CAUSES/INTERACTS_WITH->(Epstein-Barr Virus Infections)-Barr Virus Infections)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Mutation in CD21 gene -> Impaired B cell activation -> Reduced susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus infection -> 80% CHAIN: Mutation in CD21 gene -> Decreased complement receptor type 2 (CR2) expression -> Reduced susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus infection -> 75% CHAIN: Mutation in CD21 gene -> Impaired B cell co-stimulation -> Reduced susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus infection -> 70% CHAIN: Mutation in CD21 gene -> Altered immune response -> Reduced susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus infection -> 80%
enhanced_information: A mutation in the CD21 gene leads to impaired B cell activation, decreased complement receptor type 2 (CR2) expression, impaired B cell co-stimulation, and altered immune response, all of which collectively reduce susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus infection. This aligns with the standard consensus that mutations in CD21 gene can protect against Epstein-Barr virus infection. The evidence paths showing interactions between complement receptor type 2, B-lymphocytes, and Epstein-Barr virus further support this relationship.
analysis: The core medical principle here is that a mutation in the CD21 gene leads to impaired B cell activation, decreased CR2 expression, and altered immune response, which collectively reduce susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus infection. This aligns with the enhanced information provided. Rhinovirus, Human immunodeficiency virus, Cytomegalovirus, and Parvovirus are not directly affected by mutations in the CD21 gene. Therefore, the most likely correct option is Epstein-Barr virus.
